claims.text: In a regional evaluation, extended pharmacy hours were followed by a 6 percent relative fall in out-of-hours GP contacts for minor ailments and a net annual budget impact of an extra 0.4 million.
claims.passage: a net annual budget impact of an extra 0.4 million
claims.interpretation: Offsets did not cover the supplement in the one empirical costing, and staffing costs were excluded.

claims.text: A decision model found the three-year budget impact most sensitive to the share of late-night users who would otherwise have attended an emergency department.
claims.passage: Results were most sensitive to the share of late-night pharmacy consultations that would otherwise have led to an emergency department attendance
claims.interpretation: The counterfactual is the key unknown in any budget figure.

claims.text: Budget impact analyses from different health systems differ in perspective, price year, currency, horizon and offsets, and pooling them is not recommended.
claims.passage: avoid a pooled figure unless the studies share perspective and setting
claims.interpretation: The quantitative strand should use structured tables in common prices, not a pooled estimate.

claims.text: Among late-evening pharmacy users in two cities, 22 percent had no registered GP.
claims.passage: 22 percent of users had no registered GP
claims.interpretation: Late opening may reach people poorly served by general practice.

claims.text: Pharmacy owners relied on locums for late hours, and four of nine reduced their hours within a year.
claims.passage: Four of the nine owners had reduced their hours within a year.
claims.interpretation: Sustainability and staffing costs belong in both strands.

claims.text: Sunday opening was not followed by a clear change in emergency attendances for minor conditions.
claims.passage: There was no clear change in level or trend of Sunday attendances for minor conditions
claims.interpretation: Emergency department offsets may be small, at least while awareness is low.

synthesis: Eight retrieved records, appraised at abstract level. Only one empirical costing exists: offsets covered most but not all of the supplement (net extra 0.4 million a year) and excluded staffing costs above the supplement. A decision model turns on the unknown share of users who would otherwise attend an emergency department, and a time series found no clear change in such attendances after Sunday opening. Late users are younger, often shift workers, and a fifth have no registered GP. Pharmacists and owners describe lone working, fatigue and costly locums, and some schemes shrank within a year. Commissioners doubt pharmacist-estimated savings. A methods review advises against pooling budget figures across health systems.
gradeRationale: Budget evidence rests on one before-after costing and one model with expert inputs; practice evidence is qualitative and consistent. Certainty that extended hours save money is very low; certainty about who uses them and what staffing involves is low to moderate. Overall low.
summary: Eight retrieved records appraised; six source-derived claims recorded; overall certainty low.
